uncertaintyKind: DAMIT represents the published 90–92 km thermophysical fit range as 91±1 km. This is a fit range, not an independently stated one-sigma Gaussian confidence interval or a local shape-accuracy bound.
diameterSemantics: Selected DAMIT archived solution volume-equivalent diameter, independently checked against raw mesh volume.
limitations: Delbo and Tanga2009 supplementary section on Lydia explicitly choose pole1 (149.3,-55), matching model152, because it fits slightly better (reduced chi-square0.7 versus0.76). The second pole remains possible. Its IRAS thermophysical diameter range is90–92 km versus94–97 km for pole2; the archive stores91±1 km.
visibleDescription: Convex light-curve reconstruction with the thermally preferred pole and a published 90–92 km diameter fit range. The archive mesh uses 91 km; another pole remains possible. The grid marks unavailable imagery; rotational phase is illustrative.

publishedSizeInterval.interpretation: Thermophysical fit range for selected pole; publication does not label it one-sigma
publishedSizeInterval.source: Delbo and Tanga2009 supplementary results for110 Lydia
